newsitem.title: USA: AOL to mix ads with online chat sessions.
newsitem.headline: AOL to mix ads with online chat sessions.

text.p: America Online Inc said Tuesday it plans to introduce advertising to the portion of its service devoted to private online discussion, or "chat" between subscribers.
The Dulles, Va.-based company said the move will generate an additional 360 million impressions every month.
Impressions refer to the number of screens an AOL user views in an online session and are the standard measurement used by AOL to bill advertisers.
The overall number of ad impressions generated by AOL's service could not be obtained.
AOL's chat area, known as "People Connection," creates up to 14,000 virtual chat rooms with up to 23 people in one area.
The ads would appear in the public spaces of the chat area, not the chat sessions themselves.
Advertisements would rotate every 60 seconds, utilizing AOL's new ad server technology.

The online service has said it expected an increasing portion of its revenues to derive from ads instead of just subcriber fees as it transitions to become a media company from its roots as an online access company.
America Online is the world's largest Internet online service with about eight million members.

"AOL has the largest online chat community in the universe," said Bob Pittman, president of America Online Networks, AOL's main operating unit. "Over 70 percent of our members chat and we log one million hours of chat every day, a figure that has more than doubled over the last six months.
"This is yet another asset that we have that will allow AOL to capture an ever larger percentage of online and Internet advertising spending," he said.
